author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Students at Cranston High School West planted 2,977 American flags outside Alumni Auditorium on Thursday, creating a memorial for every person killed in the September 11, 2001, attacks.

The school’s Young Americans for Freedom chapter organized the display as part of the national “Never Forget” project. Students and teachers said the field of flags gives a human scale to an event that happened before today’s high-school students were born.

The installation comes as communities mark the 25th anniversary of the attacks. For students learning about September 11 as history rather than lived memory, the project turns the casualty count into a visible tribute spread across the school grounds.

The flags are scheduled to remain in place through September 12. Organizers described the display as both a remembrance and an invitation for students to ask questions about the victims, first responders and the long-term effects of the attacks. Cranston West’s project is one of many local observances planned across New England for the anniversary.
dek: The memorial outside Alumni Auditorium marks 25 years since the attacks and gives each person killed a visible place in the school display.
headline: Cranston West students plant 2,977 flags for September 11 victims
